Hi Oliver,

Thanks for the heads up and for sending the remittance. I can see the PDF but a couple of items need clarification before we post:

1) Legal entity split: because the payment originated from two Helix accounts, we need a per-invoice allocation that indicates which legal entity paid each invoice (Helix Media Ltd vs Helix Production LLP). That determines VAT treatment on our side.
2) Bank reference mapping: the BACS reference you provided (HM-5MAY-2291) appears in the bank trace, but the trace rows don't map cleanly to invoice IDs. Can you confirm the exact amount applied to HM-INV-20250520 and HM-INV-20250527?
3) FX / rounding: we saw a £0.30 difference between the gross listed in the remittance and the credited amount on our end — likely bank rounding. If you can confirm the cents/pence breakdown that would help reconciliation.

Our proposed next steps:
- If you can resend a short CSV with columns: invoice_id, amount_paid, payer_entity, vat_amount we can apply automatically.
- If not, we'll hold allocation and mark as 'pending split' by EOD Friday (2025-06-13).

I'll loop in Laura from finance for VAT treatment and Vanessa for ledger posting. If you prefer a quick call we can jump on a 15-min slot.

Best,

Jonas Weber

Summary of actions we will take today:
- Apply payments as provided in your CSV. Posting plan: HM-INV-20250512 (45,120.00 GBP) and HM-INV-20250527 (39,624.00 GBP) will be posted to Helix Media Ltd ledger; HM-INV-20250520 (38,540.50 GBP) will be posted to Helix Production LLP ledger.

- Rounding discrepancy: the £0.30 variance you flagged reconciles to bank fees/rounding; we will record a miscellaneous posting code (RCV-BNK-ROUNDS) on the applied transaction. If you prefer us to route that to a suspense account for you to clear, let us know.
